purpose: Track independence and formal architecture of prioritized historical-modern Rarámuri candidates without converting grades into cognation probabilities.

grading_rule.A: Historical evidence plus modern evidence independent of the historical editorial lineage, with external controls for the principal formal differences. Important reconstruction problems may remain.
grading_rule.A-: Strong historical-modern evidence with at least one significant independence or formal-control gap.
grading_rule.B: Plausible candidate with evidence concentrated in a dependent or unresolved modern source or with substantial uncontrolled formal differences.
grading_rule.B-: Exploratory candidate whose semantics or form remain weakly controlled.

candidates.basis: Independent Choguita documentation plus historical phonetic control for <tsch>.
<ss>=[s], historical e~i variation, modern pretonic /e/ raising, and independent Balleza community usage.
Independent <tsch>~tʃ controls, matching stress and semantic field, plus Guerrero community usage.
Independent Choguita governor form and external controls for e~i, l~r and the participial domain. A competing selígame<selaka etymology remains unresolved.
Direct historical color form plus independent multivariety modern paradigm and controlled historical affricate value.
Direct historical-modern root and color-morphology continuity with multivariety modern evidence.

Steffel explicitly places schiógameke in the blue-green domain; modern seyó/siyó is independently documented across multiple regions; historical š~s has independent controls; historical color morphology provides -cameke and -ameke~-ame controls.
open_issues: Exact treatment of the medial glide in historical schió- versus modern seyó/siyó
Historical competition and eventual fate of pamaguéameke

interpretation: All seven prioritized families now satisfy the project's Grade A architecture criterion. This closes the evidence-independence phase for this candidate set but does not establish seven demonstrated cognations.
next_phase: Move from candidate confirmation to targeted reconstruction of unresolved morphological, phonological and lexical histories.
